question: Why does the official SET validation grid residual sit at 0.3-0.6 %, and how much of it is the fixture's own lost input precision rather than an implementation error?

classification.supersedes_earlier_reading: any earlier statement that the grid residual was explained by printed-input rounding is superseded: it is not explained
classification.meaning: Index quantisation is PLAUSIBLE as the dominant cause and is quantitatively supported as a major contributor: a single set of offsets inside the +-0.5 the F8.0 columns imply removes most of the residual. It is not ESTABLISHED as the cause. The residual that remains lies above the precision the density column itself carries, and because the original index vintage is unavailable the cause of that remainder cannot be distinguished and is reported as unknown.

metric_definitions.signed_density_difference_kg_m3: density_native - density_reference, SIGNED, kg/m3. The sign carries the systematic bias and is retained deliberately.
metric_definitions.absolute_error_kg_m3: |density_native - density_reference|, kg/m3. Distinct from the signed difference above; the two are reported separately so a one-sided bias is never hidden inside a magnitude.
metric_definitions.signed_relative_error: (density_native - density_reference) / |density_reference|, sign preserved so bias is visible
metric_definitions.denominator_zero: excluded from the error statistics and counted separately; no substitute value is reported
metric_definitions.rms: root mean square over every evaluated row of this record. The full-grid record evaluates all 545528 rows; the decimated shipped test evaluates 13320 distinct rows. These are different populations and their max values differ slightly by sampling alone - see sample_populations below.
metric_definitions.signed_tinf_difference_k: native TEMP(1) - printed TINF, SIGNED, K
metric_definitions.signed_temp_difference_k: native TEMP(2) - printed TEMP, SIGNED, K

provenance.note: Per-row records carry the epoch, the full-precision evaluation point and the printed precision of every input. This block carries the file-level identity that a row inherits from its fixture_file entry.

external_distribution.redistribution: not permitted upstream; official source and validation output are used in place and never vendored here

native_kernel.role: calls the unmodified official JB2008.f directly, bypassing the C++ bridge, coordinate layer and weather loader

adapter_probe.role: same contract through the shipped Jb2008 adapter

official_astronomy.role: links the unmodified official SUNPOS and THETA sliced byte-identically from the hash-verified driver

probes.sha256_note: Probe binaries are rebuilt by reproduce.sh on every run and are not hashed here; the sources they compile from are in the repository manifest.

fixture_sha256.note: Verified by the loader in tests/jb2008_tests.cpp against the pinned digests recorded in docs/atmosphere/JB2008.md; a file whose digest does not match is a hard error, so a row's fixture_file name identifies an exact byte sequence.

provenance.row_inheritance: Every entry in stratification.worst_twenty carries its own fixture_file, epoch_utc, mjd_utc, sat_ra_rad, sun_ra_rad, sun_dec_rad and input_precision block; the fixture_file value maps to epochs[] above for the file-level hashes.

sample_populations.note: Two distinct populations are reported and must not be compared as if they were the same measurement.

full_grid.selection: every row of all eight published files

decimated_shipped_test.selection: every 41st row plus the trailing endpoint of each file; the previously reported 13328 double-counted row 0 once per epoch
decimated_shipped_test.deduplication_effect: removing the repeated row changes only the weighting: RMS 0.0032388564212367911 -> 0.0032398286550430365, max 0.0058605859224980525 unchanged. The full-grid max 0.005889466852069977 is slightly larger purely because it includes rows the 41-row decimation does not visit.

coverage.grid: 97 altitudes 120-600 km x 37 longitudes x 19 latitudes

stratification.interpretation_limits: Strata are reported for every epoch, covering altitude, latitude, longitude, time of day, DSTDTC and reference density separately. All twenty worst cases lie at the top of the grid.
stratification.causality_caveat: These strata are descriptive only. All eight epochs are three-hourly steps within a SINGLE calendar day and share one printed solar index set, so 'no dependence on latitude' means no variation was resolvable across the sampled latitudes AT THIS ACTIVITY LEVEL - it is not evidence that density error is independent of latitude. Likewise the DSTDTC and time-of-day strata span one day's geomagnetic variation and cannot separate solar-activity effects from geomagnetic ones, or disentangle time of day from epoch. No causal or independence claim is made from any stratum.

bridge_is_bit_exact.meaning: the project adapter and a direct call to the official Fortran model agree to the last bit on every evaluated row; the ABI bridge, right-ascension wrapping and domain checks add nothing

astronomy_is_not_the_cause.meaning: the driver's own THETA/SUNPOS agree with the IAU-1982 expression used by the test to well below the residual

official_astronomy_provenance.meaning: the two subroutines are the driver's own bytes, sliced from a hash-verified source; no dummy symbol is linked beside code presented as official

index_sensitivity.method: central difference of relative density at step h and h/2, each dividing the full 2*step span; Richardson extrapolation uses the central-difference rule (4*D(h/2) - D(h))/3

residual_is_one_scalar.statement: at fixed altitude the relative density error is nearly constant across all latitude/longitude points of that plane

scalar_tc_offset.interpretation: The per-epoch thermal offsets mimic most of the sampled density residual but leave disagreement above publication precision. This is a hypothetical input-sensitivity result, not recovered source data, a complete rounding explanation, or proof that a better fit is impossible; the search has finite resolution.

bounded_fit.method: coordinate descent on the true model output, every trial point re-evaluated through the unmodified official Fortran kernel; no linearisation of density in the indices is assumed
bounded_fit.bound_meaning: half-step of the fixture's F8.0 index columns; an offset inside this box is one the published precision cannot distinguish from the printed value
bounded_fit.meaning: A SINGLE set of index offsets, every one inside the +-0.5 half-step the fixture's own F8.0 columns imply, removes 92.7-97.4 % of the residual RMS. That is positive evidence that index quantisation dominates. It does NOT reach the 5e-05 relative half-ulp of the D15.5 density column, so it does not by itself account for the published numbers to print precision.

indices_h_1.0.note: Offsets are joint least-squares estimates at one epoch and are reported for the residual they remove, not as measured values: the eight indices are strongly collinear in their effect on density, so individual offsets are not identifiable.  They are not bounded by the F8.0 print either; several exceed 0.5 by orders of magnitude, which is itself evidence that the fit is absorbing collinearity.

indices_h_0.5.note: Offsets are joint least-squares estimates at one epoch and are reported for the residual they remove, not as measured values: the eight indices are strongly collinear in their effect on density, so individual offsets are not identifiable.  They are not bounded by the F8.0 print either; several exceed 0.5 by orders of magnitude, which is itself evidence that the fit is absorbing collinearity.

indices_plus_altitude_plus_latitude_h_1..note: If geometry freedom materially improved on the index-only fit, the residual would not be attributable to the printed solar indices.  Compare with indices_h_1.0.

identifiability.note: If geometry freedom materially improved on the index-only fit, the residual would not be attributable to the printed solar indices.  Compare with indices_h_1.0.

parallel_envelope_check.performed_by: altitude investigation in this same amendment
parallel_envelope_check.method: all 2**8 corners of the +-0.5 sfu index box evaluated and the sampled grid points tested for containment
parallel_envelope_check.quantity_note: FULL corner-to-corner span (high - low) / rho, NOT a half width. The upstream field name previously read 'half_width', which mislabelled the quantity; it has been corrected to max_corner_span_relative.
parallel_envelope_check.interpretation: a PER-POINT compatibility result: each sampled point is individually consistent with SOME corner of the box. It does NOT establish that one single global input vector inside the box reproduces the whole grid, which is the stronger claim tested by bounded_fit above and not confirmed there.
parallel_envelope_check.note: Complementary, not competing: the envelope bounds which points are individually admissible, while bounded_fit tests whether a single admissible set works globally and leaves a residual above print precision.

unresolved.issue: the residual remaining after the best in-bound index fit
unresolved.explanation: The bounded nonlinear search did not find a single input set reproducing its sampled rows to print precision. This does not prove that no such set exists: optimisation may be incomplete. Other original-input, model-version or producer-compiler differences are also untested because the dated full-precision inputs and producer build settings are unavailable. Complete causal attribution remains UNRESOLVED; no original values are inferred from the fit.

unresolved.issue: the full-precision index record behind the 2023 fixture
unresolved.explanation: The current SOLFSMY.TXT is a different data vintage from the one that produced the fixture. Its values differ from the published F8.0 row in nearly every index by far more than the +-0.5 half-step, and using them directly is roughly 54 times worse, which confirms a vintage mismatch rather than recovering the original. The underlying values are therefore stated as unknown; only their bounded effect is claimed.

unresolved.issue: independent activity inference from this grid
unresolved.explanation: All eight epochs share one printed solar index set and span only DSTDTC in {24, 50, 85, 115} within a single calendar day, so solar-activity dependence cannot be separated from geomagnetic variation here.

what_would_resolve: obtaining the 2023 SOLFSMY vintage, so the printed F8.0 index row could be replaced by its full-precision original and the residual re-measured against a known input
an independently reconstructed input set that accounts for the grid to within the D15.5 print precision, which would confirm or refute the residual-above-print-floor item
redistribution: No official SET source or data is vendored or copied into this repository. JB2008.f is compiled in place from the hash-pinned external path; SUNPOS and THETA are sliced byte-identically from a hash-verified driver into a scratch file. All probe code in the repository is project-owned and reproduces no JB2008 equation.
